# renew

> renew is an open-source game engine written in Rust, licensed Apache-2.0. Its
> simulation core is bit-deterministic by construction: a fixed timestep over integer
> nanoseconds, arithmetic in Q47.16 fixed point, no wall-clock reads, no unseeded
> randomness, and no iteration-order-dependent state. Rendering goes through an internal
> RHI backed by Vulkan via `ash`. Every capability is a library with a command-line face
> that emits schema-versioned JSON, so a person, a script, or an agent drives the engine
> through the same surface.

renew is in early development (pre-0.1). APIs are unstable and no module has reached
`stable` maturity. It is not yet ready to build a game on. The project is developed in the
open at https://github.com/renew-engine/renew.

## Key facts

- Name: renew (also written "renew engine"); organization `renew-engine` on GitHub.
- Language: Rust, edition 2024, stable toolchain 1.97 or newer.
- License: Apache-2.0.
- Platforms: Windows, Linux, macOS desktop.
- Graphics: Vulkan through the `ash` crate, behind an internal RHI whose public API names
  no Vulkan type. MoltenVK on macOS.
- Windowing: `winit`, behind a default-on feature on the platform crate.
- Structure: 26 engine crates, 5 of them core; every non-core crate is removable, and CI
  builds and tests one configuration per removed crate to prove it.
- Determinism scope: simulation code only. Presentation-side crates (cameras, particle
  rendering, UI rendering) interpolate at display rate and are outside the digest.

## Crates

- renew-diag — log records, severity levels, and the sink interface (internal, core)
- renew-event — the event vocabulary as plain data, no dependencies (internal, core)
- renew-math — Vec2/3/4, Mat4, Quat, Aabb3 with documented layout (internal, core)
- renew-memory — LinearArena, generation-checked Pool<T>, counting global allocator (internal, core)
- renew-platform — the engine's only doorway to the OS: clock, files, threads, window (internal, core)
- renew-fixed — Q47.16 fixed-point arithmetic for reproducible simulation
- renew-frame — the fixed-timestep accumulator over integer nanoseconds
- renew-ecs — sparse-set component storage with a defined iteration order
- renew-jobs — a fixed-size worker pool with deterministic-chunk parallel_for
- renew-rng — PCG32 with derived per-domain streams
- renew-input — input state and action mapping over the event vocabulary
- renew-replay — record a run to an input trace, replay it, compare digests
- renew-trace — the input-trace codec and simulation digests
- renew-physics2d — bodies, shapes, broadphase, SAT narrowphase, raycasts, sweeps, slide resolution
- renew-physics3d — the same surface in three dimensions, axis-aligned only
- renew-rhi — the GPU doorway: Vulkan through ash behind an engine interface
- renew-render2d — sprites from an atlas, one instanced draw
- renew-render3d — indexed geometry, depth-tested, in submission order
- renew-camera — look-at view, reversed-depth perspective, inter-tick blending
- renew-snapshot — two captures of one slot space blended by the interpolation factor
- renew-particles — a fixed-capacity particle pool stepped at the simulation cadence
- renew-ui — a retained widget tree solved in fixed point inside the simulation
- renew-ui-render — retained snapshots blended at display rate, emitted as sprites
- renew-audio — a fixed-voice mixer and WAV reader behind the platform's device seam
- renew-asset — content-addressed asset packs, every entry verifiable against its digest
- renew-png — PNG encoding with no dependencies

## Command-line surface

One binary, `renew`, drives the workspace: `configure`, `build`, `test`, `bench`, `run`,
`record`, `replay`, `lint`, `check`, `coverage`, `modules`, `asset-pack`, `asset-inspect`,
`determinism`, `doctor`. Every command accepts `--json` and emits a single
schema-versioned document.

## Disambiguation

"AI-first", as the project uses the term, means every capability is headless, scriptable,
and machine-operable. It does not mean the engine ships AI features.

renew is not related to the unrelated `renew` crate on crates.io (a deployment daemon),
nor to any subscription, licence, or passport renewal service.
